\subsection{Artifact 14: Do Borrowed Ideas Stick When Grafted Locally?}

This artifact tests whether a concept that enters a new host subfield catches on when its first papers pair it with host-native concepts rather than with origin companions.
Pre-registration frozen before any outcome (sha256 \texttt{f800a0a9\ldots}).

\textbf{Setup.} 4,177 main-arm host entries (concept~$c$ first appears in non-origin subfield~$d$ in year~$e$).
Primary sample: 1,740 screen MAIN entries with $\geq 5$ partners, in 184 concepts.
Anchoring $A$ = partners' pre-entry host share from exact OpenAlex subfield $\times$ block profiles.
Co-transfer CT = share of partners that were origin companions in $[e{-}5, e{-}1]$.
Only 1.1\% of partner tags are $\geq 50$\% host-native, so the pre-declared fallback makes continuous $A_{\mathrm{cont}}$ primary.

\subsection{Artifact 15: How New Concepts Spread---Types, Roles, Timing}

\subsubsection{Diffusion Typology}

3-channel diffusion typology (rarefied Shannon, Rao-Stirling, active subfields; Hennig bootstrap $B = 200$).
Only $k = 2$ is stable (min Jaccard 0.861): \textbf{localised} ($n = 136$) and \textbf{broad from the start} ($n = 66$).

\begin{table}[!htbp]
\centering
\caption{Diffusion typology summary (Artifact~15, Iteration~3).}
\label{tab:typology}
\begin{tabularx}{\textwidth}{lrYl}
\toprule
Cluster & $n$ & Description & Dominant origin \\
\midrule
Localised & 136 & Low entropy, few active subfields throughout & Physics \\
Broad from start & 66 & High entropy and many subfields from early years & Mixed \\
\bottomrule
\end{tabularx}
\end{table}

\begin{figure}[!htbp]
  \centering
  \includegraphics[width=\linewidth,height=0.85\textheight,keepaspectratio]{figures/fig_typology_cases_v0.pdf}
  \caption{Representative cases of the $k = 2$ diffusion typology: localised ($n = 136$, top row, blue) and broad-from-the-start ($n = 66$, bottom row, orange). Each row shows the cluster's medoid (left) and the nearest non-medoid concept (right). Localised concepts stay near-monopolised by a single subfield (88--97\%, entropy 0.14--0.40~nats). Broad concepts split across two or more subfields from their first window (entropy 0.79--1.24~nats).}
  \label{fig:typology_cases}
\end{figure}

The entropy-only baseline typology is stable at finer $k = 4$ (Jaccard 0.856).
After residualising on early volume, the 3-channel typology does NOT separate unclustered outcomes better than the entropy-only baseline (newcomer share $\varepsilon^2$ 0.171 vs 0.178).

\subsubsection{Community Roles}

Leiden community roles with 5-seed agreement (97.2\% robust, placebo 0.87): BRIDGE 0.61, OTHER 0.33, STAYER 0.03, MIGRANT 0.02.
Lagged roles do not robustly predict host-subfield entry: BRIDGE OR 0.64 [0.38, 1.08].

\subsubsection{Expansion Precedes Diffusion}

In 15 of 16 concepts exhibiting both an expansion onset and a diffusion onset, expansion precedes diffusion (proportion 0.94 [0.81, 1.0], year-shuffle null 0.62, $p = 0.004$).

\subsection{Dead Ends and Negative Results (Iteration 3)}

\begin{enumerate}
\item \textbf{Openness does not predict WHERE concepts travel.} Breadth-prediction screen: all Holm $p = 0.405$.
\item \textbf{Brokerage is not the mechanism behind low closure.} Burt constraint is higher, not lower ($S = +0.083$ [0.017, 0.147]).
\item \textbf{The 3-channel diffusion typology adds nothing beyond entropy.} $\varepsilon^2$ 0.171 vs 0.178.
\item \textbf{Community roles do not predict host entry.} BRIDGE OR 0.64 [0.38, 1.08].
\item \textbf{Co-transfer is null.} Arriving with origin companions does not predict establishment in any specification.
\end{enumerate}

\subsection{Strategy}

Iteration~4 is a CONFIRMATION iteration.

\subsubsection{Held-Out Confirmation of Descriptive Findings}

Five pre-registered expectations were tested on the held-out fold:
\begin{itemize}
\item \textbf{Typology shares.} PASS: BROAD share 0.35 vs 0.33.
\item \textbf{Type $\times$ outcome association.} PASS: 3/3 Kruskal-Wallis tests significant.
\item \textbf{Expansion-first ordering.} PASS: 10/10 on held-out.
\item \textbf{Anchoring $\times$ typology interaction.} FAIL: BRIDGE OR flips sign (0.64 screen vs 1.86 held-out).
\item \textbf{Other descriptive patterns.} PASS.
\end{itemize}

\subsubsection{Rooting: Do Broad Concepts Anchor More?}

NOT SUPPORTED.
Screen mean $A_{\mathrm{cont}}$ difference: $-0.0018$; held-out: $+0.0005$, CI including zero.
However, BROAD concepts do have lower co-transfer: CT difference $-0.125$ [$-0.19$, $-0.06$] on the held-out fold.

\subsection{Artifact 20: Adopter-Level Mechanism}

This artifact tests whether authors who adopt a concept in a new host subfield had prior corpus exposure to the concept's entry partners.
The test uses conditional logistic regression on 1,013 matched case-control strata (422 entries, 109 concepts) from the screen fold.

\subsection{Artifact 24: Positioning Dossier}

Novelty verdict: \textbf{PARTLY ANTICIPATED} (0 ANTICIPATES, 11 PARTLY among 25 graded candidates).
No located work measures how host-specific the vocabulary is that a concept is combined with when it enters a new subfield, and relates that, within concepts and across hosts, to later uptake by the host's own newcomers.
The nearest work (Cheng et al.\ 2023) measures global embeddedness of new ideas ($+1$~SD $\to$ approximately $+25$\% articles) using a multilevel over-dispersed Poisson model with a global word2vec embedding.
The margin held by this study is: host-specific context at entry, concept fixed effects across hosts, author-disjoint newcomer outcome, sealed-fold confirmation, and MeSH replication.

%% ====================================================================
\section{What the Run Learned Overall and What Is Still Open}
\label{sec:conclusion}
%% ====================================================================

\subsection{Confirmed Findings}

\textbf{Host-entry grafting predicts durable integration (RQ2).}
When a concept enters a new host subfield, the share of its initial co-occurrence partners that are native to that host predicts subsequent uptake by newcomer authors.
The co-primary held-out estimate is IRR/SD $= 1.19$ [1.06, 1.33] ($p = 0.0045$), the MeSH replication gives IRR/SD $= 1.23$ [1.12, 1.36] (Holm $p = 9.7 \times 10^{-5}$), and the IVW pooled estimate is 1.26 [1.17, 1.36] with $I^2 = 0$.
The effect operates through both the extensive margin (IVW $+6.43$~pp/SD) and the intensive margin (IVW IRR/SD 1.183).
It is host-specific (IVW retention 0.969 after generality controls), does not vary by origin field (Wald $p = 0.638$), and is labelled ``host-vocabulary'' by the discriminating tests.
Co-transfer of origin companions is null across all folds and populations.

\textbf{Persistent-neighbour closure is confirmed (RQ1, secondary).}
Among stable top-20 associates, emerging concepts have lower triadic closure before onset (held-out $S = -1.073$, Holm $p = 0.015$).
Burt constraint replicates its positive sign, ruling out a structural-holes explanation.

\textbf{Diffusion typology.}
The $k = 2$ typology (localised vs broad-from-the-start) replicates on the held-out fold.
Network expansion precedes disciplinary diffusion in 25 of 26 pooled main-arm dual-onset concepts.

\textbf{Adopter mechanism.}
Adopters are enriched for prior exposure to the concept's entry partners (OR 3.09), with the gradient FOREIGN $>$ ADJACENT $>$ NATIVE, consistent with absorptive capacity or topical proximity.

\subsection{Dead Findings}

\begin{itemize}
\item \textbf{Primary closure (R1\_DEAD).} Holm $p = 0.147$ on held-out. The general closure deficit does not survive confirmation.
\item \textbf{Source-sink viability (C0).} Blocked by Gate~A failure (within-host traced share 0.17).
\item \textbf{Breadth prediction.} Openness does not predict where concepts travel beyond growth baselines.
\item \textbf{Closure-anchoring link.} Null ($\rho = 0.049$). The two findings (closure and grafting) are independent.
\item \textbf{Community roles predicting host entry.} BRIDGE OR 0.64 [0.38, 1.08].
\end{itemize}

\subsection{Open Questions}

\begin{enumerate}
\item The population is dominated by physics/CS arXiv concepts. Generalisation to social sciences and humanities is untested.
\item The primary fully-saturated specification is underpowered on the held-out fold and MeSH. Only the co-primary specification supports the grafting claim.
\item The binary establishment threshold ($\mathrm{EST}_{\mathrm{bin}}$) is null on the held-out fold.
\item Single-paper entries (87\% of screen co-primary events) drive the effect more strongly on the held-out fold. The pooled multi-team effect is positive but the held-out alone is inconclusive.
\item The adopter-level vocabulary gradient (FOREIGN $>$ NATIVE) runs opposite to the entry-level finding (host-native partners predict uptake). Whether these reflect different mechanisms at different scales or a single mechanism with a selection effect is unresolved.
\item The 3-channel diffusion typology adds nothing beyond entropy trajectories. Whether richer trajectory features can yield a more informative typology is untested.
\item 292 numbers present in artifact output files were not transcribed into the report (audit finding). Full transcription was not attempted.
\end{enumerate}

\end{document}

(b)~Co-word network: 25 yearly co-occurrence snapshots ($\\approx$27{,}000 nodes, $\\approx$84{,}000 edges) partitioned into Leiden communities. (c)~Analysis: RQ1 (emergence) tests structural precursors with a closure event study. The primary closure test returns R1\\_DEAD, while persistent-neighbour closure is confirmed. RQ2 (diffusion) tests host-entry grafting, which is confirmed (IRR/SD $=1.19$ on the held-out fold and MeSH). Its sub-hypotheses K1 (BOTH margins) and K2 (HOST-SPECIFIC) are supported, and K3 finds no field boundary. (d)~Diffusion typology: a $k=2$ solution separating localised concepts (136) from concepts broad from the start (66).}\n  \\label{fig:methodology}\n\\end{figure}\n\n%% ====================================================================\n\\section{Iteration 1: Data Foundation and Pre-Registration}\n\\label{sec:iter1}\n%% ====================================================================\n\n\\subsection{Strategy}\n\nThe first iteration was devoted to three preparatory tasks: (a)~assembling a prior-art and pre-registration dossier grading each candidate mechanism's novelty and feasibility, (b)~building the concept pool and its associated OpenAlex work corpus, and (c)~constructing the semantic grounding infrastructure (concept detection, labelling, variant merging) and a held-out MeSH confirmation population.\nNo experiment or evaluation was executed.\nEvery artifact in this iteration is either a dataset or a research dossier.\nThe rationale was to fix all operational definitions, sample the data, and verify the citation-layer gate (Gate~A) before committing compute to network construction and statistical modelling.\n\nThe pre-registration dossier ranks five candidate mechanisms by novelty margin against the nearest prior work.\nHost anchoring (the share of a concept's new co-occurrence edges in a host subfield that attach to host-native concepts) was ranked highest at medium-to-high novelty.\nToolkit co-transfer was ranked high on measurement novelty but coupled to host anchoring.\nCitation-lineage source-sink viability was ranked medium.\nOrigin-neighbourhood structure was ranked low-to-medium, and the demic-versus-cultural adoption channel was ranked medium but with the weakest feasibility due to author-disambiguation biases.\n\nA pre-registered screen was fixed before any data were inspected.\nThe unit of analysis is a concept~$c$ in non-origin subfield~$d$ at focal year~$t$ (2010--2014), with at least 10 $d$-papers in $W_1 = [t{-}5, t]$.\nThe primary measure is out-of-sample ROC-AUC for establishment in $W_2 = [t{+}1, t{+}5]$, where establishment means at least 5 $W_2$ $d$-papers by author-disjoint newcomers and presence in at least 3 of the 5 $W_2$ years.\nThe BASE model includes $W_1$ edge volume, momentum, concept age, subfield-year size, concept total volume, concept entropy, subfield count, growing-edge breadth, Rafols integration, relatedness density and Maillart-style features.\nEach candidate adds only its own pre-registered scores.\nA candidate survives if its delta-AUC over BASE has a concept-bootstrap (1,000 reps) 95\\% CI lower bound above~0, its point gain is at least 0.01, and the coefficient sign matches its prediction.\n\n\\subsection{Artifact 1: Concept Pool and OpenAlex Work Corpus}\n\\label{sec:artifact1}\n\nThe concept pool was built in an outcome-blind frame.\nThe sample was frozen and hashed (SHA-256 \\texttt{80e3f244\\ldots0c44}) before any post-appearance-window data were inspected.\nThe pool comprises 206 concepts, of which 184 are main emerging concepts (first appearance year~$F$ in 2005--2016, with 20--300 papers in the window $F$ to $F{+}2$ and no more than 8,000 total works through 2024) and 22 stationary reference concepts.\nThe 184 main concepts are split by a SHA-1 hash into a screen fold of 123 and a held-out concept fold of 61, focal-year tags are separate (screen 2010--2014, held-out 2016--2018).\n\nThe pool is heavily dominated by arXiv-sourced concepts.\nOf 366 eligible candidates, 363 came from the arXiv-mined arm, and the final 184 span three origin fields.\n\n\\begin{table}[!htbp]\n\\centering\n\\caption{Concept pool composition by origin field (Artifact~1, Iteration~1).}\n\\label{tab:pool_origin}\n\\begin{tabular}{lrr}\n\\toprule\nOrigin field & Main concepts & Share \\\\\n\\midrule\nPhysics and Astronomy & 82 & 44.6\\% \\\\\nPhysical the 121,829 main-arm links, 56,997 matched in the work title, 51,966 in the abstract, 10,177 through Semantic Scholar only, and 2,689 through OpenAlex concept indexing alone.\n\\emph{[Correction, Among the 184 main concepts the split is 24 native and 160 S2-mapped.]}\nTwenty-one concepts carry a sense-check failure flag.\n\n\\subsubsection{Gate A: Citation-Layer Feasibility}\n\nThe quality report shows that among main-arm concept papers with references, 66.99\\% cite at least one earlier concept paper (the ``traced share''), and after excluding first-year canonical papers and the five most-cited concept papers, the traced share remains 60.80\\%.\nThe host-specific traced share is 55.18\\%, above the 40\\% gate threshold on the lenient definition.\n\\emph{[Correction, Iteration~2: the original description stated ``at least one earlier concept paper in the same host subfield'', but the code counts any earlier concept paper as a parent regardless of subfield. It was computed from each source's all-years OpenAlex topic counts, which come from the same citation-reading topic classifier whose temporal label leakage the dossier flagged. An ASJC journal-level habitat was built in Iteration~2 as a replacement, though its coverage is only 12.1\\% of concept-work links.]}\n\n\\subsection{Artifact 2: Whole-Science Background Sample}\n\nA design-weighted background sample of 259,716 OpenAlex works from 1,260 strata (150 per field $\\times$ year, weights summing to 149,116,575) was built to supply co-occurrence network snapshots and calibrate host-nativeness profiles.\n\\emph{[Correction, Iteration~5: Artifact~2 is the workspace \\texttt{gen\\_art\\_dataset\\_2}.]}\nIt delivered 6,325 exact subfield $\\times$ year totals and 400 exact concept $\\times$ block subfield profiles for 100 calibration concepts at a cost of \\$0.1952 in OpenAlex credits.\n\nThe key finding of this artifact is negative: sample-based per-concept subfield profiles are unreliable for determining host-nativeness.\nIn the calibration table, the median total-variation distance between sample and exact profiles is 0.41--0.79 by frequency decile, and top-subfield agreement is only 0.28--0.65.\nThis means host-nativeness and the concept-concept background network cannot be computed reliably from this sample alone, and require paid exact profiles.\nAbout 12\\% of the weighted frame carries the default low-confidence topic T14423, and concept ancestors are no longer served by the API.\nThe worker timed out after writing all outputs (no new JSONL records for 2,096~seconds), so its status is ``failed'' while its data are usable.\n\n\\subsection{Artifact 3: Held-Out MeSH Confirmation Population}\n\nA separate biomedical confirmation arm was built from new MeSH descriptors (DateEstablished 2006--2016, widened to 2004--2005 and 2017--2018).\nStarting from 28,472 descriptors, the pipeline selects 5,201 topical descriptors, retains 3,430 after the provenance filter, narrows to 283 passing the PubMed novelty pre-screen and early-volume rule, and adds widening-pool candidates.\nAfter the final rule, 191 concepts survive: 99 core 2006--2016, 14 from the 2004--2005 widening, and 78 from the 2017--2018 widening.\n\n\\begin{table}[!htbp]\n\\centering\n\\caption{MeSH held-out population by branch group (Artifact~3, and Shortfalls (Iteration 1)}\n\n\\begin{enumerate}\n\\item \\textbf{Concept pool size.} 184 of 400 target concepts realised. The binding constraint was the free-singleton retrieval rate ($\\sim$14 works/s) combined with heavy-tailed concept sizes, after credits were consumed by sibling artifacts sharing one key.\n\n\\item \\textbf{Field coverage.} The pool draws overwhelmingly from physics, physical sciences, and computer science (363 of 366 eligible candidates from the arXiv-mined arm). The OpenAlex keyword/taxonomy arm had a 2.2\\% eligibility yield (3 of 134 candidates) because OpenAlex tags are retroactive.\n\n\\item \\textbf{Survivorship-free phrase pool yield.} 1 of 150 target strict-eligible anchored concepts.\n\n\\item \\textbf{Labelling quality.} Silver labels only (no human check). Model~A's bias is moderate, Model~B over-labels CONCEPT (1,333 of 1,491 items vs A's 882).\n\\end{enumerate}\n\n\\subsection{What Was Learned (Iteration 1)}\n\nIteration~1 established the data foundation and pre-registration.\nThe concept pool of 184 main emerging concepts and 22 reference concepts, with 214,798 verified concept-to-work links and 208,374 unique works, passes the citation-layer gate on the lenient (any-parent) definition but has not been tested at the within-host edge level required for viability estimation.\nThe MeSH held-out population of 191 biomedical concepts provides a secondary check arm, though with caveats on completeness and ground-truth quality.\nNo experiment was executed.\nNo quantitative result about the hypothesis exists.\n\n\n%% ====================================================================\n\\section{Iteration 2: Gates, Viability, Emergence Event Study}\n\\label{sec:iter2}\n%% ====================================================================\n\n\\subsection{Strategy}\n\nIteration~2 was a FIX iteration.\nFive goals were set: (i)~complete the hydration and add exact nativeness profiles and a citation-independent venue habitat; (ii)~train and evaluate the concept grounding pipeline; (iii)~compute Gate~A as written (within-host, non-canonical, per $W_1$ year) and estimate viability states with synthetic validation and pre-outcome power; (iv)~build the yearly concept-concept co-occurrence network and run the RQ1 event study; (v)~replicate the RQ1 event study on the MeSH population.\n\nPre-fixed decision rules for Iteration~3: (a)~if Gate~A FAILS, H1/H2 run with graft labels from the exact nativeness profiles; (b)~H1 is declared a pilot if fewer than $\\sim$150 concepts carry a tested edge; (c)~RQ1 counts as CONFIRMED only if at least one pre-named precursor has an event-study CI excluding~0 AND a delta-AUC CI excluding~0 on the main screen fold, keeps its sign on MeSH, and holds on the sealed held-out fold; (d)~the held-out fold, the 2016--2018 focal years and the phrase pool remain untouched.\n\n\\subsection{Artifact 6: Hydrated Corpus, Nativeness Profiles, and Venue Habitat}\n\nThis artifact completes the hydration of the concept pool from 184 to 426 concepts (366 main: screen 247, held-out 119, 60 reference), with 462,812 works and ====================================================================\n\n\\subsection{Strategy}\n\nIteration~3 deepens the closure lead from the emergence question and carries the recombination mechanism into cross-disciplinary diffusion at two scales.\nThe strategy (``Is it brokerage, and does grafting make it stick?'') has four components: (i)~an evaluation artifact that audits every number in the Iteration-2 report and runs a turnover pre-check; (ii)~a deeper test of the emergence question on the hydrated 247-concept screen fold with turnover-proof openness measures; (iii)~a breadth-prediction screen; (iv)~a host-entry grafting test; and (v)~a descriptive diffusion experiment.\n\n\\subsection{Artifact 11: Record Audit and Turnover Pre-Check}\n\nThis artifact reads all five Iteration-2 artifacts and audits every reported number against the raw output files.\n\\textbf{Numbers of record:} 406 rows were audited, 182 recomputed from item-level files.\nThere are 42 non-OK drift flags: 14 WRONG\\_ESTIMATOR, 10 WRONG\\_UNITS, 9 WRONG\\_DEFINITION, 8 DRIFT\\_VALUE, 1 NOT\\_REDERIVABLE.\n\n\\begin{table}[!htbp]\n\\centering\n\\caption{Turnover pre-check: \\\\\nIVW pooled & -- & $-0.186$ [$-0.453$, 0.081] & Ambiguous ($Q$ 1.88, $I^2$ 0.47) \\\\\n\\bottomrule\n\\end{tabularx}\n\\end{table}\n\nThe residualised effect retains approximately two-thirds of the raw effect (not reducible to turnover alone), but the CI includes zero.\n\n\\subsection{Artifact 12: Is Openness Before Take-Off Brokerage or Churn?}\n\nThis artifact re-attaches all 426 hydrated before labels.\n\n\\textbf{Populations.} After applying the frozen replacement rule (180 sense values filled): MAIN screen 202 (102 old, 100 new), held-out 100, STRICT 196/96, SENS finer $k = 4$ (Jaccard 0.856).\nAfter residualising on early volume, the 3-channel typology does NOT separate unclustered outcomes better than the entropy-only baseline (newcomer share $\\varepsilon^2$ 0.171 vs 0.178).\n\n\\subsubsection{Community Roles}\n\nLeiden community roles with 5-seed agreement (97.2\\% robust, placebo 0.87): BRIDGE 0.61, OTHER 0.33, STAYER 0.03, MIGRANT 0.02.\nLagged roles do not robustly predict host-subfield entry: BRIDGE OR 0.64 [0.38, 1.08].\n\n\\subsubsection{Expansion Precedes Diffusion}\n\nIn 15 of 16 concepts exhibiting both an expansion onset and a diffusion onset, expansion precedes diffusion (proportion 0.94 [0.81, 1.0], year-shuffle null 0.62, $p = 0.004$).\n\n\\subsection{Dead Ends and Negative Results (Iteration 3)}\n\n\\begin{enumerate}\n\\item \\textbf{Openness does not predict WHERE concepts travel.} Breadth-prediction screen: all Holm $p = 0.405$.\n\\item \\textbf{Brokerage is not the mechanism behind low closure.} Burt constraint is higher, not lower ($S = +0.083$ [0.017, 0.147]).\n\\item \\textbf{The 3-channel diffusion typology adds nothing beyond entropy.} $\\varepsilon^2$ 0.171 vs 0.178.\n\\item \\textbf{Community roles do not predict host entry.} BRIDGE OR 0.64 [0.38, 1.08].\n\\item \\textbf{Co-transfer is null.} Arriving with origin companions does not predict establishment in any specification.\n\\end{enumerate}\n\n\n%% ====================================================================\n\\section{Iteration 4: Held-Out Confirmation and Replication}\n\\label{sec:iter4}\n%% \documentclass[11pt,letterpaper]{article}
\usepackage{graphicx, geometry, amsmath, hyperref, url, booktabs, xcolor, tabularx}
\geometry{margin=1in}
\hypersetup{colorlinks=true, linkcolor=black, citecolor=black, urlcolor=black}
\usepackage[T1]{fontenc}
\usepackage[utf8]{inputenc}

\newcolumntype{Y}{>{\raggedright\arraybackslash}X}

\title{Executive Summary\\[4pt]
\large Open Neighbourhoods Precede Concept Spread:\\
Structural Antecedents and Cross-Disciplinary Diffusion\\
of Emerging Scientific Concepts}
\author{}
\date{September 2026}

\begin{document}
\maketitle

%% ─────────────────────────────────────────────────
\section*{Headline}
%% ─────────────────────────────────────────────────

When a scientific concept enters a new subfield, the share of its initial co-occurrence partners that are native to that host predicts whether the concept will be taken up by the host's own newcomer authors.
The effect replicates on a held-out concept fold (IRR/SD 1.19 [1.06, 1.33], $p = 0.004$) and an independent MeSH biomedical population (IRR/SD 1.23 [1.12, 1.36], Holm $p < 0.001$), pools to IRR/SD 1.26 [1.17, 1.36], operates through both extensive and intensive margins, and is host-specific rather than reflecting general concept accessibility.

%% ─────────────────────────────────────────────────
\section*{Goal}
%% ─────────────────────────────────────────────────

The study investigates two questions using an OpenAlex-based scholarly dataset of 426 semantically grounded concepts with 462,812 works:

\begin{description}
\item[RQ1 (Emergence)] Which temporal and structural patterns in an evolving, semantically grounded scientific knowledge graph characterise the emergence of scientific concepts?
\item[RQ2 (Diffusion)] How do emerging scientific concepts diffuse across disciplinary communities over time, and which temporal network patterns distinguish locally concentrated concepts from broadly integrated ones?
\end{description}

The target venue is \emph{Applied Network Science}.

%% ─────────────────────────────────────────────────
\section*{What Was Tried}
%% ─────────────────────────────────────────────────

Five iterations over 25 artifacts:

\begin{enumerate}
\item \textbf{Data foundation (Iteration~1).} Built a concept pool of 426 concepts (366 main, 60 reference), 462,812 works, and 488,078 verified concept-work links from OpenAlex with a held-out MeSH confirmation population of 191 biomedical concepts. Pre-registered all decision rules and hashed specifications before data inspection.

\item \textbf{Gates, viability, and emergence event study (Iteration~2).} Tested the citation-layer gate (Gate~A) at edge level; built 25 yearly co-word network snapshots ($\sim$27,000 nodes, $\sim$84,000 edges); ran the RQ1 precursor event study on the screen fold and MeSH population. Originally planned source-sink viability estimation; blocked by Gate~A failure.

\item \textbf{Deepen closure, test grafting, describe diffusion (Iteration~3).} Deepened the closure finding with turnover-proof openness measures. Tested host-entry grafting on 1,740 screen-fold entries using PPML regression. Built a $k{=}2$ diffusion typology and tested expansion-before-diffusion ordering.

\item \textbf{Held-out confirmation and replication (Iteration~4).} Opened four sealed held-out folds. Confirmed the co-primary grafting specification. Replicated on MeSH. Tested single-paper artefact, vocabulary decomposition, classifier circularity, closure-anchoring link, and adopter-level mechanism.

\item \textbf{Post-confirmation decomposition, audit, positioning (Iteration~5).} Ran three K-tests: margin decomposition (both extensive and intensive confirmed), host-specificity (confirmed), and field boundary (no variation). Full numerical audit (319 curated numbers, 99.4\% accuracy). Positioning dossier grading novelty against 25 candidates.
\end{enumerate}

%% ─────────────────────────────────────────────────
\section*{Key Results}
%% ─────────────────────────────────────────────────

\begin{table}[!htbp]
\centering
\small
\caption{Summary of confirmed and dead findings.}
\begin{tabularx}{\textwidth}{lYl}
\toprule
Finding & Evidence & Status \\
\midrule
Host-vocabulary grafting (RQ2) & Co-primary IRR/SD: screen 1.30, held-out 1.19, MeSH 1.23; IVW pooled 1.26 [1.17, 1.36] & CONFIRMED \\
Margin decomposition (K1) & Extensive IVW $+$6.43 pp/SD; intensive IVW IRR/SD 1.183 & BOTH \\
Host-specificity (K2) & IVW retention 0.969; $A_{\mathrm{lift}}$ IVW IRR/SD 1.34 [1.23, 1.46] & HOST-SPECIFIC \\
Field boundary (K3) & Wald $p = 0.638$ & NO VARIATION \\
Persistent-neighbour closure (RQ1) & Held-out $S = -1.073$, Holm $p = 0.015$ & CONFIRMED \\
Diffusion typology ($k{=}2$) & Localised (136) vs broad-from-start (66); replicates on held-out & CONFIRMED \\
Expansion before diffusion & 25 of 26 pooled dual-onset concepts & CONFIRMED \\
Adopter enrichment & OR 3.09 [2.32, 4.28]; gradient FOREIGN $>$ ADJACENT $>$ NATIVE & CONFIRMED \\
\midrule
Primary closure (R1) & Holm $p = 0.147$ on held-out & R1\_DEAD \\
Source-sink viability (C0) & Gate~A failure: within-host traced share 0.17 & BLOCKED \\
Breadth prediction & All Holm $p = 0.405$ & NOT SUPPORTED \\
Closure-anchoring link & Partial $\rho = 0.049$, $p = 0.564$ & NULL \\
\bottomrule
\end{tabularx}
\end{table}

%% ─────────────────────────────────────────────────
\section*{What Failed}
%% ─────────────────────────────────────────────────

\begin{itemize}
\item \textbf{Gate~A (citation-layer feasibility).} Only 17.3\% of host edge-years meet the within-host tracing threshold (vs 64.2\% under lenient any-parent tracing). The viability decomposition central to the original hypothesis could not be executed.
\item \textbf{Primary closure (R1\_DEAD).} The general closure deficit does not survive held-out confirmation (Holm $p = 0.147$). Only the persistent-neighbour variant survives.
\item \textbf{Breadth prediction.} Openness does not predict where concepts travel beyond growth baselines.
\item \textbf{Community roles.} Leiden community roles (BRIDGE, STAYER, MIGRANT) do not predict host-subfield entry (BRIDGE OR 0.64 [0.38, 1.08]).
\item \textbf{Co-transfer.} Arriving with origin companions is null across all folds and populations.
\item \textbf{Concept pool field coverage.} 363 of 366 eligible candidates from the arXiv arm; social sciences and humanities are absent.
\end{itemize}

%% ─────────────────────────────────────────────────
\section*{Open Questions}
%% ─────────────────────────────────────────────────

\begin{enumerate}
\item \textbf{Generalisability.} The population is dominated by physics/CS arXiv concepts. Extension to social sciences and humanities is untested.
\item \textbf{Primary specification power.} The fully-saturated primary specification is underpowered on the held-out fold and MeSH. Only the co-primary specification supports the grafting claim.
\item \textbf{Establishment threshold null.} The binary establishment threshold ($\mathrm{EST}_{\mathrm{bin}}$) is null on the held-out fold ($+$2.54 pp, $p = 0.16$).
\item \textbf{Single-paper dominance.} 87\% of screen co-primary events are single-paper entries; the held-out interaction ($p = 0.004$) suggests the effect is stronger for single-paper entries.
\item \textbf{Adopter-vs-entry paradox.} The adopter-level vocabulary gradient (FOREIGN $>$ NATIVE) runs opposite to the entry-level finding (host-native partners predict uptake). Whether these reflect different mechanisms at different scales is unresolved.
\item \textbf{Audit residuals.} 292 numbers in artifact outputs were not transcribed into the report. Seeded-perturbation recall is 0.60.
\end{enumerate}

\end{document}

Only persistent-neighbour closure is confirmed (held-out S = -1.07, Holm p = 0.015). The effect is not\\n  Burt brokerage (constraint is higher, not lower). For RQ2, when a concept enters a new host subfield, the share of its initial\\n  co-occurrence partners that are native to that host predicts subsequent uptake by newcomer authors (held-out co-primary\\n  IRR/SD 1.19 [1.06, 1.33], p = 0.004, MeSH replication IRR/SD 1.23 [1.12, 1.36], Holm p < 0.001), while co-transfer of origin\\n  companions is null. Post-confirmation decomposition shows the effect operates through both extensive (IVW +6.43 pp/SD [4.76,\\n  8.11]) and intensive margins (IVW IRR/SD 1.183 [1.104, 1.267]), is host-specific rather than reflecting general accessibility\\n  (IVW retention 0.969 after generality controls, Balassa-index A_lift IVW IRR/SD 1.34 [1.23, 1.46]), and does not vary by\\n  origin field (Wald p = 0.638). A data-derived k = 2 diffusion typology separates localised from broad-from-the-start concepts,\\n  and network expansion precedes disciplinary diffusion in 25 of 26 pooled dual-onset concepts. Adopters are 3.1 times more\\n  likely than matched non-adopters to have prior exposure to the concept's entry partners, with enrichment strongest for origin-vocabulary\\n  (FOREIGN) partners.\\npaper_text: |+\\n  # Open neighbourhoods precede concept spread: structural antecedents and cross-disciplinary diffusion of emerging scientific concepts\\n\\n  This report documents an investigation of how emerging scientific concepts can be identified and characterised through evolving knowledge networks, and through which structural pathways they spread across disciplinary boundaries. The study builds on an OpenAlex-based scholarly dataset of 426 semantically grounded concepts with 462,812 works, constructs yearly co-occurrence and concept-discipline networks, and tests whether structural indicators provide early signals of emergence and cross-disciplinary integration.\\n\\n  Two research questions structure the work. RQ1 asks which temporal and structural patterns in an evolving, semantically grounded scientific knowledge graph characterise the emergence of scientific concepts. RQ2 asks how emerging scientific concepts diffuse across disciplinary communities over time, and which temporal network patterns distinguish locally concentrated concepts from concepts that become broadly integrated into the scientific knowledge network.\\n\\n  The study began with a source-sink viability hypothesis adapted from population ecology [1], asking whether a concept's presence in a subfield is self-sustaining or import-dependent. That hypothesis was blocked by insufficient citation-layer density (Gate A failure: only 17.3% of edges meet the within-host tracing threshold). The investigation followed the pre-registered fallback.\\n\\n  For the emergence question (RQ1), the primary closure measure did not survive held-out confirmation (R1_DEAD under the frozen kill rule: Holm p = 0.147). Structural precursors of sustained uptake are volume and churn correlates. Only persistent-neighbour closure survives (Holm p = 0.015).\\n\\n  For the diffusion question (RQ2), when a concept enters a new host subfield, the share of its initial co-occurrence partners that are native to that host predicts subsequent uptake by newcomer authors (held-out co-primary IRR/SD 1.19 [1.06, 1.33], p = 0.004. MeSH replication IRR/SD 1.23 [1.12, 1.36], Holm p < 0.001), while the share of origin companions does not. The effect operates through both the extensive margin (starting uptake) and the intensive margin (scaling uptake), is host-specific rather than a proxy for general concept accessibility, and does not vary detectably by origin field. A data-derived diffusion typology separates concepts into localised and broad-from-the-start trajectories, and network expansion precedes disciplinary diffusion in 25 of 26 pooled main-arm concepts exhibiting both transitions.\\n\\n  The target venue is Applied Network Science, whose published work on knowledge diaspora [6], disciplinary roles in field-of-study networks [7], alluvial community change [8], and the epistemic integration of AI in neuroscience [9] provides the closest comparison base.\\n\\n  ---\\n\\n  # Iteration 1\\n\\n  ## Strategy\\n\\n  The first iteration was devoted to three preparatory tasks: (a) assembling a prior-art and pre-registration dossier grading each candidate mechanism's novelty and feasibility, (b) building the concept pool and its associated OpenAlex work corpus, and (c) constructing the semantic grounding infrastructure (concept detection, labelling, variant merging) and a held-out MeSH confirmation population. No experiment or evaluation was executed. Every artifact in this iteration is either a dataset or a research dossier. The rationale was to fix all operational definitions, sample the data, and verify the citation-layer gate (Gate A) before committing compute to network construction and statistical modelling.\\n\\n  The pre-registration dossier ranks five candidate mechanisms by novelty margin against the nearest prior work. Host anchoring (the share of a concept's new co-occurrence edges in a host subfield that attach to host-native concepts) was ranked highest at medium-to-high novelty, toolkit co-transfer (the fraction of a concept's origin companions that co-appear in host papers) was ranked high on measurement novelty but coupled to host anchoring, citation-lineage source-sink viability was ranked medium, with Kuhn et al.'s meme propagation score [10], Kiss et al.'s epidemic diffusion model [11], De Domenico et al.'s author-flow source-sink indices [6], and Maillart et al.'s endogenous-exogenous decomposition [5] as the nearest antecedents. Origin-neighbourhood structure (the participation coefficient and clustering topology of the concept in its birth subfield) was ranked low-to-medium because structural diversity and community spread are well studied [12], and the demic-versus-cultural adoption channel was ranked medium but with the weakest feasibility due to author-disambiguation biases \\\\footnote{Code: \\\\url{https://github.com/ai-inventor-papers/ai-invention-8892b7-occupancy-is-not-integration-for-new/tree/fork/run_-5obKGrJFD0H/round-1/research-1}}.\\n\\n  A pre-registered screen was fixed before any data were inspected. The unit of analysis is a concept c in non-origin subfield d at focal year t (2010-2014), with at least 10 d-papers in W1 = [t-5, t]. The primary measure is out-of-sample ROC-AUC for establishment in W2 = [t+1, t+5], where establishment means at least 5 W2 d-papers by author-disjoint newcomers and presence in at least 3 of the 5 W2 years. The BASE model includes W1 edge volume, momentum, concept age, subfield-year size, concept total volume, concept entropy, subfield count, growing-edge breadth, Rafols integration, relatedness density and Maillart-style features. Each candidate adds only its own pre-registered scores. A candidate survives if its delta-AUC over BASE has a concept-bootstrap (1,000 reps) 95% CI lower bound above 0, its point gain is at least 0.01, and the coefficient sign matches its prediction. The candidate with the largest lower CI bound is the winner.\\n\\n  ## Artifact 1: concept pool and OpenAlex work corpus\\n\\n  The concept pool was built in an outcome-blind frame. The sample was frozen and hashed (SHA-256 80e3f244...0c44) before any post-appearance-window data were inspected \\\\footnote{Code: \\\\url{https://github.com/ai-inventor-papers/ai-invention-8892b7-occupancy-is-not-integration-for-new/tree/fork/run_-5obKGrJFD0H/round-1/dataset-1}}. The aii-paper-writing skill's style rules are the\\n  house style here too: they are about how sentences work, not about selling a result, and a\\n  report written to them is still the complete, chronological, unsold record.\\n</report_rules>\\n\\n<report_text>\\ntitle: >-\\n  Open neighbourhoods precede concept spread: structural antecedents and cross-disciplinary diffusion of emerging scientific\\n  concepts\\nabstract: >-\\n  We investigate how emerging scientific concepts spread across disciplinary boundaries using 426 semantically grounded concepts\\n  and 462,812 works from OpenAlex. Two research questions structure the work: RQ1 asks which structural patterns characterise\\n  concept emergence, and RQ2 asks how concepts diffuse across disciplinary communities. The original source-sink viability\\n  hypothesis was blocked by insufficient citation-layer density (Gate A: 17.3% within-host traced share), triggering a pre-registered\\n  fallback. For RQ1, the general closure deficit did not survive held-out confirmation on the primary operationalisation (R1_DEAD:\\n  Holm p = 0.147). Only persistent-neighbour closure is confirmed (held-out S = -1.07, Holm p = 0.015). The effect is not\\n  Burt brokerage (constraint is higher, not lower). For RQ2, when a concept enters a new host subfield, the share of its initial\\n  co-occurrence partners that are native to that host predicts subsequent uptake by newcomer authors (held-out co-primary\\n  IRR/SD 1.19 [1.06, 1.33], p = 0.004, MeSH replication IRR/SD 1.23 [1.12, 1.36], Holm p < 0.001), while co-transfer of origin\\n  companions is null. Post-confirmation decomposition shows the effect operates through both extensive (IVW +6.43 pp/SD [4.76,\\n  8.11]) and intensive margins (IVW IRR/SD 1.183 [1.104, 1.267]), is host-specific rather than reflecting general accessibility\\n  (IVW retention 0.969 after generality controls, Balassa-index A_lift IVW IRR/SD 1.34 [1.23, 1.46]), and does not vary by\\n  origin field (Wald p = 0.638). A data-derived k = 2 diffusion typology separates localised from broad-from-the-start concepts,\\n  and network expansion precedes disciplinary diffusion in 25 of 26 pooled dual-onset concepts. Adopters are 3.1 times more\\n  likely than matched non-adopters to have prior exposure to the concept's entry partners, with enrichment strongest for origin-vocabulary\\n  (FOREIGN) partners.\\npaper_text: |+\\n  # Open neighbourhoods precede concept spread: structural antecedents and cross-disciplinary diffusion of emerging scientific concepts\\n\\n  This report documents an investigation of how emerging scientific concepts can be identified and characterised through evolving knowledge networks, and through which structural pathways they spread across disciplinary boundaries. The study builds on an OpenAlex-based scholarly dataset of 426 semantically grounded concepts with 462,812 works, constructs yearly co-occurrence and concept-discipline networks, and tests whether structural indicators provide early signals of emergence and cross-disciplinary integration.\\n\\n  Two research questions structure the work. RQ1 asks which temporal and structural patterns in an evolving, semantically grounded scientific knowledge graph characterise the emergence of scientific concepts. RQ2 asks how emerging scientific concepts diffuse across disciplinary communities over time, and which temporal network patterns distinguish locally concentrated concepts from concepts that become broadly integrated into the scientific knowledge network.\\n\\n  The study began with a source-sink viability hypothesis adapted from population ecology [1], asking whether a concept's presence in a subfield is self-sustaining or import-dependent. That hypothesis was blocked by insufficient citation-layer density (Gate A failure: only 17.3% of edges meet the within-host tracing threshold). The investigation followed the pre-registered fallback.\\n\\n  For the emergence question (RQ1), the primary closure measure did not survive held-out confirmation (R1_DEAD under the frozen kill rule: Holm p = 0.147). Structural precursors of sustained uptake are volume and churn correlates. Only persistent-neighbour closure survives (Holm p = 0.015).\\n\\n  For the diffusion question (RQ2), when a concept enters a new host subfield, the share of its initial co-occurrence partners that are native to that host predicts subsequent uptake by newcomer authors (held-out co-primary IRR/SD 1.19 [1.06, 1.33], p = 0.004. MeSH replication IRR/SD 1.23 [1.12, 1.36], Holm p < 0.001), while the share of origin companions does not. The effect operates through both the extensive margin (starting uptake) and the intensive margin (scaling uptake), is host-specific rather than a proxy for general concept accessibility, and does not vary detectably by origin field. A data-derived diffusion typology separates concepts into localised and broad-from-the-start trajectories, and network expansion precedes disciplinary diffusion in 25 of 26 pooled main-arm concepts exhibiting both transitions.\\n\\n  The target venue is Applied Network Science, whose published work on knowledge diaspora [6], disciplinary roles in field-of-study networks [7], alluvial community change [8], and the epistemic integration of AI in neuroscience [9] provides the closest comparison base.\\n\\n  ---\\n\\n  # Iteration 1\\n\\n  ## Strategy\\n\\n  The first iteration was devoted to three preparatory tasks: (a) assembling a prior-art and pre-registration dossier grading each candidate mechanism's novelty and feasibility, (b) building the concept pool and its associated OpenAlex work corpus, and (c) constructing the semantic grounding infrastructure (concept detection, labelling, variant merging) and a held-out MeSH confirmation population. No experiment or evaluation was executed. Every artifact in this iteration is either a dataset or a research dossier. The rationale was to fix all operational definitions, sample the data, and verify the citation-layer gate (Gate A) before committing compute to network construction and statistical modelling.\\n\\n  The pre-registration dossier ranks five candidate mechanisms by novelty margin against the nearest prior work. Host anchoring (the share of a concept's new co-occurrence edges in a host subfield that attach to host-native concepts) was ranked highest at medium-to-high novelty, toolkit co-transfer (the fraction of a concept's origin companions that co-appear in host papers) was ranked high on measurement novelty but coupled to host anchoring, citation-lineage source-sink viability was ranked medium, with Kuhn et al.'s meme propagation score [10], Kiss et al.'s epidemic diffusion model [11], De Domenico et al.'s author-flow source-sink indices [6], and Maillart et al.'s endogenous-exogenous decomposition [5] as the nearest antecedents. Origin-neighbourhood structure (the participation coefficient and clustering topology of the concept in its birth subfield) was ranked low-to-medium because structural diversity and community spread are well studied [12], and the demic-versus-cultural adoption channel was ranked medium but with the weakest feasibility due to author-disambiguation biases \\\\footnote{Code: \\\\url{https://github.com/ai-inventor-papers/ai-invention-8892b7-occupancy-is-not-integration-for-new/tree/fork/run_-5obKGrJFD0H/round-1/research-1}}.\\n\\n  A pre-registered screen was fixed before any data were inspected. The unit of analysis is a concept c in non-origin subfield d at focal year t (2010-2014), with at least 10 d-papers in W1 = [t-5, t]. The primary measure is out-of-sample ROC-AUC for establishment in W2 = [t+1, t+5], where establishment means at least 5 W2 d-papers by author-disjoint newcomers and presence in at least 3 of the 5 W2 years. The BASE model includes W1 edge volume, momentum, concept age, subfield-year size, concept total volume, concept entropy, subfield count, growing-edge breadth, Rafols integration, relatedness density and Maillart-style features. Each candidate adds only its own pre-registered scores. A candidate survives if its delta-AUC over BASE has a concept-bootstrap (1,000 reps) 95% CI lower bound above 0, its point gain is at least 0.01, and the coefficient sign matches its prediction. The candidate with the largest lower CI bound is the winner.\\n\\n  ## Artifact 1: concept pool and OpenAlex work corpus\\n\\n  The concept pool was built in an outcome-blind frame. The sample was frozen and hashed (SHA-256 80e3f244...0c44) before any post-appearance-window data were inspected \\\\footnote{Code: \\\\url{https://github.com/ai-inventor-papers/ai-invention-8892b7-occupancy-is-not-integration-for-new/tree/fork/run_-5obKGrJFD0H/round-1/dataset-1}}.
